attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post, endorsed.

semantics.note: Keeps the 'does not appear' wording and the cloud/app-store comparison. 'Does not appear' describes how things looked then, not a probability, so it can be checked. The attached forecast about markets punishing investors is a separate claim and is rightly left out.

contract.note: Reading the claim as the visible picture in H1 2024 is fair and ordinary. Because 'easy business returns' has no measure, the result depends on that reading and on whose returns count (Nvidia earned big returns from chips). The contract says so.

evidence.note: Sequoia analysis from June 2024, before the post. It estimates a widening gap between AI spending and the revenue needed to justify it.
Goldman Sachs research from late June 2024, just before the post. It says gen AI spending had little to show for it so far.
AI added 7 points to Azure growth. That is real revenue, but it does not show easy returns relative to investment, so it does not contradict the claim.

reviews.rationale: Two credible analyses from just before the post (Sequoia, Goldman) found AI investment had produced little return so far. That matches the claim that easy returns were not visible. Microsoft's AI-driven Azure growth shows some revenue, not broad returns that cover the investment. The ungraded market forecast is excluded.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post, endorsed.

semantics.note: Restates the compound sentence faithfully. The 'so...that' clause describes a state of affairs as it stood, so observation fits. Evaluative words ('superficially impressive doodad') are not graded.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair: the main check is whether firms tempered salespeople's expectations because of cost and reliability. Reading 'remarkably unprofitable' as high cost relative to value is reasonable, since he refers to the underlying technology, not a company's accounts. No profit or loss figure is available.

evidence.note: Blog reproduction, with attribution, of The Information's March 2024 report. Cloud providers were tempering salespeople's expectations because hype exceeded what the technology delivers at a reasonable price.
Same report. It names Microsoft, AWS and Google and cites high running costs and accuracy shortcomings, matching 'unprofitable and unreliable'.
AI added 7 points to Azure growth, which supports the 'can sell cloud compute access' part. It is revenue only, not profitability.

reviews.rationale: Reporting from H1 2024 (The Information, via a faithful reproduction) says major cloud providers were tempering salespeople's expectations, citing cost and accuracy limits. That matches the main factual part. The Azure figures confirm generative AI was selling cloud compute. Nothing in the packet shows the technology was clearly profitable and reliable then. 'Unprofitable' rests on cost reports, not a loss figure.
